messages:
sara_support: Hi team — AcmeCorp (Dedicated, private VPC) reporting streaming responses cut off mid-payload, then client reconnects and we see duplicated tokens billed + truncated JSON in logs. Customer says it started after their network team upgraded an edge proxy last week.

nina_cs: added screenshots + raw client logs to the ticket. Response body ends with partial JSON like '{\"choices\": [ {\"delta\":...' then connection closes. :grimacing:

sara_support: Key details from customer: region eu-west-1, Dedicated pool d-az2, model rdx-13b-v1, auth via token rotation every 10m, client is internal Node service behind corp-proxy. They see 200 then stream stops, client reconnects, receives overlapping chunk containing duplicated suffix.

packetbot: Deploy note: last infra change in that Dedicated cluster 2024-11-02 03:12 UTC — kernel patch + haproxy 2.6. Storing event.

tom_eng: Can you paste a minimal client repro? Also need pcap or tcpdump at their edge and our ingress.

acme_ops: Repro steps we ran: 1) curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=rdx-13b-v1\" 2) send prompt with long streaming output (tokens ~3k). 3) midway our corp proxy posted a ~RST then we reconnect. Node client stacks: 'eventsource-polyfill' + retry on close. We see duplicate suffix and partial JSON.

ben_runtime: Sounds like mid-payload TCP segmentation + proxy buffering is delivering duplicate chunks on reconnect. Two quick asks: capture pcap on client side (before proxy) and on our ingress. Also give exact content-length/transfer-encoding headers seen.

raj_neteng: From Acme's packet capture snippet they sent: lots of retransmits and MSS clamping by proxy, plus WINDOW_UPDATE bursts. Proxy is doing TLS termination and a sticky connection pool to our ingress; when it times out it replays last N bytes to another backend connection. That's a red flag.

nina_cs: Customer attached our server-side logs: 
```
[ingress] conn 0x7f9f2e: sse payload chunk 512 bytes written
[ingress] conn 0x7f9f2e: client closed connection during write: EPIPE
[auth] token rotated for session xxxxxx
[ingress] conn 0x7f9f33: resumed stream for session xxxxxx, replay offset -128
[billing] session xxxxxx charged token-range 1200-1800
[ingress] conn 0x7f9f33: final chunk truncated: unexpected EOF while parsing JSON
```

nina_cs: They also included the proxy config snippet where keepalive_timeout is 20s and maxidle 50, and http-reuse is on.

tom_eng: Two parallel hypotheses: 1) Corp-proxy is buffering/rewriting chunks and on failover it replays buffered tail resulting in duplicate bytes. 2) Token rotation + reconnect race: new connection uses rotated token and server starts a new session that overlaps with previous billing window. Both could produce truncated JSON + duplicate billing.

ben_runtime: Action plan: (a) request full pcap from Acme's pre-proxy interface and our TLS terminator (b) reproduce in lab by inserting an nginx reverse proxy that replays last N bytes on backend failover, (c) add server-side defensive check to drop duplicate-overlap by monotonic stream offsets, (d) short-term customer workaround: set proxy tcp_nodelay on and disable backend connection replay/keep-alive pool to avoid chunk replay.

raj_neteng: In addition, ask Acme to temporarily increase MTU/disable MSS clamping and set keepalive to >60s to avoid mid-chunk timeouts. Also check that proxy isn't doing chunked body reconstruction (some appliances will reassemble before sending).

acme_ops: We can provide pcaps and will try keepalive change. One question: why do we see billing for duplicate tokens? Shouldn't dedup happen?

ben_runtime: Our billing currently charges on emission of token batches. If a reconnect causes the same token content to be emitted again (server restarted segment), we may double-count. We'll add an internal ticket to consider idempotency keys per session to dedupe within a sliding window. For now, we'll correlate with request IDs to issue credits where applicable.

tom_eng: Quick repro snippet for internal lab (nginx to emulate corp proxy):
```
# nginx conf (proxy that buffers and may replay tail on backend fail)
proxy_buffering on;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_send_timeout 10s;
keepalive_timeout 20s;
```
Then run a curl streaming client and kill the backend connection mid-chunk to see behavior.

sara_support: I've asked Acme for: pcaps (pre-proxy + post-proxy), exact proxy model/version, and their retry logic. I've also escalated to eng-runtime and billing to start a credit investigation.

ben_runtime: I'll spin up a local repro today and post results. If we can reproduce, we'll push a short-term server-side guard: detect resumed sessions with overlapping offsets and prefer the higher-offset stream, dropping earlier duplicates (logs + metrics).

nina_cs: Customer acknowledged and will try keepalive change + send pcaps. They asked for an ETA on credits.

sara_support: ETA for credit audit: 48h after we receive pcaps + request ids. I'll update ticket when I have the files. Thanks all. :handshake:
